rule: No process-global mutable state in production code: statics with interior mutability, thread-local slots, environment or working-directory reads at the point of use, process-wide hooks and child processes that inherit the live environment. Pass state through configuration and context instead, read the process's arguments and environment once at the entry point, and spawn children with env_clear() plus an explicit environment. check_process_globals.py fails on anything unlisted and on entries that no longer match, so this list only shrinks. 'debt' entries are scheduled for removal (dev-docs/ProcessGlobalsPlan.md in the glade-wz workspace); 'permanent' entries are reads at a program's entry point, items that carry no shared state (such as a temp-name counter), and spawns that clear the environment, env_clear() plus an explicit environment: the checker lists every Command::new whether or not it clears the environment, and gwz-core records its own clean spawn the same way.
source: scripts/checks/check_process_globals.py is gwz-core's checker at commit 730e7119 (gwz-dev workspace), vendored byte for byte; its own tests live there.

entries.name: env::args
entries.reason: The program reads its arguments once, at its entry point, and passes them down.

entries.name: env::vars_os
entries.reason: The program captures its whole environment once, at its entry point, and passes it down; gwz runs with env_clear() plus it (ProcessGlobalsPlan Step 3.2).

entries.name: Command::new
entries.reason: exec::command, the one place glade-gwz builds a gwz command (the blocking runner spawns it, the streamed verb converts it to tokio's), spawns gwz with env_clear() plus the environment main captured. The checker lists every Command::new, so a spawn that clears the environment is recorded as permanent, as gwz-core records its own (ProcessGlobalsPlan Step 3.2).
